newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INDUSTRY SAYS MANY JOBLESS UNFIT FOR WORK.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INDUSTRY SAYS MANY JOBLESS UNFIT FOR WORK.

text.p: The Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT) said on Friday that many jobless construction workers were unfit for work and that many of them lacked the will to work.
"Most of the unemployed in the building sector are not employable by means of (labour office) placement nor even with the help of short-term targeted training," TT said in a statement.

The industry lobby based its views on a recent survey -- conducted by it and building industry associations and labour authorities -- of the prospects to employ jobless construction workers in the Helsinki metropolitan area.

Of 91 unemployed floor-covering workers surveyed, only about 10 were immediately suitable for work, and about a further 10 could be made fit for work after one or two months of further training, TT said.

"According to the joint assessment by the officials and employers (participating in the survey), the rest of the job-seekers were completely unemployable in the floor-covering sector -- and a significant number of them unemployable in any sector," it said.

Though "back, knee and hand disabilities, cardiovascular diseases and dust allergies" among many of the over 40-year-old jobless workers made them unfit for work, they were still counted as unemployed job-seekers, TT said.
"It is important to distinguish precisely between social security and unemployment security," it said.

"A significant number of the jobless workers (in the survey) did not show up at all for job interviews or could not be contacted. Some of the job-seekers were skilled workers in other trades, such as masons or painters," TT said.
Not one jobless worker had taken the initiative to look for work by personally visiting companies in the business, it said.
The survey demonstrated the need to bring labour exchange services and the data on job-seekers up to date and to improve the unemployment security system, TT said.
"Poste restante addresses should not be accepted ... Those who are not available to the job market should be removed from the ranks of job-seekers," TT said.
